chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī, from ʿAlī, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The husband may perform ghusl for his wife during travel, and the woman [may perform ghusl for] her husband during travel, if there is no man with them.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This ruling regarding the man and the woman is only permitted when no one other than the two of them is found. But in a case of choice and the presence of women or men, that is not permissible in any circumstance. What we have previously presented of the reports indicates this, and what he narrated further clarifies it:

key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: a situation of choice rather than necessity

ai.seo_question: Can a husband or wife wash their deceased spouse during travel if no one else is present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the washing of a deceased spouse during travel when no one else is available. The accompanying statement of Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan restricts this allowance to necessity and explains that it is not permitted when other suitable men or women are present.
